title: Adam Kadmon: the will for a will, created like a language
overview:
Chapter 18 explains the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*. The last level of the *ratzon kadum*, the will for the final finished thing, becomes the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, which is called *Adam d'Beriya* and thought: a new creation, a something that expresses the true nothing.

Rabbi Walters reads *Adam Kadmon* as association. A person's essential will, for a home or to be kind, says nothing yet about a house or a coat. He has to build a self-image and a worldview, a language inside the will, that tells him what he wants; that connection is the *ratzon l'ratzon*. It is created, not essential: business and learning come and go, connections can be strong or weak, and a bribe can make one. The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are such hidden associations, the source of the revealed wills of *Atzilus*: G-d decided to reveal Himself as wise, as a creator, as a king. They come from the *Kav*, yet they are only one of the ways the *ratzon kadum* could come out. The *Kav* itself is above all association, knowing everything by knowing itself.

terms.gloss: the preceding will: an essential will for oneself, like the will for a home, not yet for anything outside
the man of Beriya: Adam Kadmon, which at the general level corresponds to thought and to creation
something from nothing: a new thing, a form that expresses the true, simple nothing
a will for a will: the created association that connects an essential will to a particular thing
enclothed: the will once thought has associated it with a particular thing, like a coat
a bribe: it connects the judge's own will to one side, so his mind is no longer objective
a screen: an interface, like a language, that connects a light so it can be given over
the joining of courtyards for Shabbos: what connects people who each have their own whole path
hidden thought: the subconscious association from which the wills of Adam Kadmon come
self-knowledge: since you know yourself, you know what you want; the ratzon kadum, as against Adam Kadmon

sections.title: The Keser of Adam Kadmon: the last level of the primordial will becomes something new
sections.summary: The *Malchus* of the *ratzon kadum*, the will for the final finished thing, becomes the *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is called *Adam d'Beriya* and thought, because it is a creation *yesh me'ayin*: a something that expresses the true nothing, the *Or Ein Sof* in the *Kav*.

phrases.he: (יח) והנה בחינת רצון הקדום לעצמו, כל מה שיהיה בהשתלשלות,
שכלול מי' עד בחינת סוף מעשה שעלה ברצון קדום זה,
phrases.en: has the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* until the *sof maaseh*, which is the *ratzon* for the final finished thing

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אחרונה שבו
הרי מבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון כו'
phrases.en: from *Malchus* of a higher level becomes the *Keser* of a lower level

blocks.text: Here, in chapter 18, the Mitteler Rebbe (Rabbi DovBer of Lubavitch, the author) is going to explain the *yosher* (the straight line) of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world). Then in chapter 19 he will explain the relationship of *Adam Kadmon* to the lights that come out in *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation).

This *ratzon* (will), the original *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will), is like the will for a home: it is really what you want to get out of the whole *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), this whole process of your will. So it is not yet a will for something outside of you. It is a will for you to get something. Now you want it to come from something outside of you, but you are still really thinking about what you are going to get from it, not about the thing itself that is going to give it to you.

And as we said, it **has the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* until the *sof maaseh***: the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) of the *igulim* (circles), down to the *sof maaseh* (the end of the deed), which is **the *ratzon* for the final finished thing**.

And so **from *Malchus* of a higher level becomes the *Keser* of a lower level**. That is the general way it always works: from the *Malchus* (kingship) of the *igulim* comes the *Keser* (crown) of *Adam Kadmon*. More particularly there is an enclothing at different levels, but that is the general rule.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: And this becomes *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: להיות ידוע דבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה דרך כללות,
phrases.en: when you're speaking of the general worlds, *Adam Kadmon* is called the *Adam d'Beriya*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת המחשבה
phrases.en: and that's *machshava*

phrases.he: ועתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות
phrases.en: the *Keser* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: נקרא אדם דיצירה,
phrases.en: is called the *Adam d'Yetzira*

phrases.he: וזעיר אנפין ונוקבא אדם דעשיה כו'
phrases.en: *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* of *Atzilus* is called *Adam d'Asiya*

blocks.text:
**And this becomes *Keser* of the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.** It is known that **when you're speaking of the general worlds, *Adam Kadmon* is called the *Adam d'Beriya***, the man of *Beriya* (the world of Creation), **and that's *machshava*** (thought). In general, *Beriya* corresponds to thought, *Yetzira* (the world of Formation) to *dibur* (speech), and *Asiya* (the world of Action) to *maaseh* (action).

So too here, at the general level. In a *mashal* (analogy), the general level is the *hishtalshelus* within a person's will, inside himself, to figure out what he wants. Then the *hishtalshelus* of the details is figuring out how to get what he wants, how to do it.

In general the *hishtalshelus* repeats itself over and over again: the same things just become more and more broken up into detail. So once you start to get a big picture, you start to see how everything kind of corresponds to everything else. And yet there is a unique aspect in each thing that you have to highlight, and then see how it exists at each stage. So this is like thought.

*Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (lit. the Ancient of Days and the long countenance) of *Atzilus*, that is, **the *Keser* of *Atzilus***, **is called the *Adam d'Yetzira***. And *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* (lit. the small countenance and the female) of *Atzilus* are called *Adam d'Asiya*. Because within your will, the final stage is when your will becomes a particular thing, and then it is able to affect your body: you will have some emotional reaction, as will be explained when we get down to it.

phrases.he: וכמו שהבריאה היא התהוות יש מאין ממש כידוע,
phrases.en: And just like a creation is something new, something *yesh me'ayin*, means that it wasn't there, something from nothing

phrases.he: כך גם בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון זה נקרא בריאה יש מאין
phrases.en: So too *Adam Kadmon* is now something new.

phrases.he: האמיתי דאור אין סוף עצמו שבקו
phrases.en: it's a *yesh* coming from the true *ayin*

phrases.he: הנזכר לעיל הנקרא רצון קדום לעצמו כו'.
phrases.en: the *Or Ein Sof* that's in the *Kav* is called the *ratzon kadum* for Himself

blocks.text: **And just like a creation is something new**, *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), meaning that it was not there before, **so too *Adam Kadmon* is now something new**: it takes the original will and makes it into something new. It is a *yesh* (something) coming **from the true *ayin*** (nothing): the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) in the *Kav* (the ray of light) is the true nothing, because it is totally simple.

The true *ayin* is the *Or Ein Sof*: the revelation of G-d is totally simple and transcends any form. Now it is coming to be revealed in a form, so this is a *yesh*, a something that expresses the nothing. That is the general idea of *yesh me'ayin*. And **the *Or Ein Sof* that's in the *Kav* is called the *ratzon kadum* for Himself**.

sections.title: Adam Kadmon is association: the self-image that turns an essential will into a will for a will
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is the source of every *ratzon l'ratzon*, and the *ratzon l'ratzon* is in *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is like the self-image and worldview a person creates, a language within the will that tells him what he wants; it is the picture of the perfect world and the perfect person, *Moshiach*.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע,
phrases.en: so now we're going to explain

phrases.he: להיות מבואר למעלה דרצון קדום הנזכר לעיל הוא הנקרא מקור כל הרצונות
phrases.en: This *ratzon kadum* that we spoke about in the last two chapters is the source for all the *ratzonos* that come out in this *hishtalshelus*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת רצון ההיולי
phrases.en: this is like an essential *ratzon*

phrases.he: להיות ממנו נמצא מקור לכל רצון לרצון
phrases.en: the source for every *ratzon l'ratzon*

blocks.text: **So now we're going to explain.** **This *ratzon kadum* that we spoke about in the last two chapters is the source for all the *ratzonos*** (wills) **that come out in this *hishtalshelus***. It is the *hiyuli* (raw potential) will, **an essential *ratzon***, and so it is **the source for every *ratzon l'ratzon*** (a will for a will). The *ratzon l'ratzon* is in *Adam Kadmon*.

The basic idea of *Adam Kadmon*, as he is going to explain now, is that it is like when a person creates a self-image for himself, and also a worldview: an image of how everything in the world relates to him. He takes his essential will, like the will for a home, to feel a certain way, and it becomes a will for a house. Included in that, he will have to have a will to work, to make the money to pay for the house, and a will for all the actual details of how it will come out. Those depend on his circumstances, the world he is in, his society, and the nature of reality in the world he finds himself in. The way a person associates his essential will with the world around him: that is done in *Adam Kadmon*.

So there are really two things. There is his goal, like the guy sitting in 770 planning out his dream. It is inside himself, it is what he wants, but it is an abstract thing. Then you have to look at the world around you and create an image of what would fit this will; that creating is what is like *Beriya*. As we said before about the guy who sits down with the architect. The architect says, "Well, what, tell me what you like." "Well, I like to swim." "Okay, that means you want a swimming pool."
blocks.title: The dreamer in 770 and the architect

blocks.text: You have to create a new will. We are still talking within the will: his will now has to take on a tangible form. The basic idea of *Adam Kadmon* is association. That is the general idea of thought and of *Beriya*: you take a will or an idea and associate it with something. Like when you create a language: what do you do? You take a certain sound, a certain shape, whatever it is, and you associate it with an idea, and now you express this idea through this word. That is what thought does when it creates a language. Here, within the will, you have to create a language within yourself, so that you know what you want.

So you have to say, "Well, when I..." A baby starts off with a pain in its stomach when it is hungry. It has to learn to associate that with the desire to eat, and then it knows. This process, which goes on at first just to figure out what it is that you want, is the roots of the wills.
blocks.title: The hungry baby

blocks.text: When you connect an essential will with other wills, that is a *ratzon l'ratzon*: the desire now becomes a desire for something else. If you are hungry, that is going to mean you want food. If you want food, that means you will have to put on your shoes, walk down to the store and buy something; and before you can do that, you will have to have a will to work, to make the money to get it. Whatever it is. The way all these wills get put together is really an understanding you create of how things work in the world around you.

Based on that understanding, whenever you have a will, it plugs it in and creates a tangible will out of it. The same with a person who has an inner will, say, to be connected to G-d, or to be *Chassidish*, or whatever it is. He creates a self-image of his goal: "I want to be a person like this." He sees himself as an *oved* (one who serves G-d) or a *maskil* (a person of intellect) or whatever; he creates some kind of image, and that becomes his life goal.

This is what it says, that *Adam Kadmon* is like the seventy years of a person's life. A person creates an image of the perfect him and of everything around him, which is his life goal. His inner desires, for fulfillment, for tranquility and the rest, come from the *ratzon kadum*, and he turns them into a picture of a utopian experience in the world he is in.

As we said, the *ratzon kadum* is the original will for the *sof maaseh*, the will for the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). And *Adam Kadmon*, in the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for), creates the form of *Moshiach*. That is what it says: *Adam Kadmon* is *Moshiach*, the picture of the perfect world. But that is the *chitzoniyus* (the outer side) of *Adam Kadmon*. The *pnimiyus* (the inner side) of *Adam Kadmon* is the picture of the perfect person, *Moshiach* himself. He represents "and I will dwell within them": the real dwelling is within a person, the way a person would be when he is totally fixed up.

And now we are coming to Yud-Tes Kislev. This is the idea of what it says, that the Alter Rebbe was a new soul. All the souls were first included in *Adam HaRishon*: almost all souls are included in his soul, and they are like details coming out of him. Therefore they are already somewhat stuck in the world. That is the whole *mashal* of the pit: the guys that were stuck in a pit, and then they threw down a new guy. The whole point of that *mashal* was that most souls are brought up already believing in the world somewhat. Even *tzaddikim* (the righteous) are stuck somewhat within the reality of the *hishtalshelus* and the world and everything.
blocks.title: Yud-Tes Kislev: the Alter Rebbe, a new soul

blocks.text: A *Moshiach* soul, and there are a few of them, like Chanoch and Eliyahu and then the Alter Rebbe, is one that was higher than *Adam HaRishon*. Such a soul comes into the world and is never trapped by associating G-d's will with a certain form. It feels the inner thing and sees the G-dliness in everything right away, and the inner goal, and how everything is just a means to accomplish it. So it is never trapped or fooled by the particular form something is associated with, never gets stuck, and never loses sight of the real *metzius* (existence) of things.
blocks.title: A Moshiach soul is never trapped by a form

sections.title: The example of kindness: the urge at the door, and the coat it is enclothed in
sections.summary: The *yechida*'s desire for kindness first goes out as a *ratzon kadum*: an urge, still for himself, that the crying man at the door should feel good. Only when thought evaluates the situation and associates it with a coat is it enclothed as a *ratzon l'ratzon*, and that is like a new creation.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך דוגמא מבחינת יחידה שבנפש האדם,
phrases.en: this is like the *yechida* of a person's soul, is like the *etzem hanefesh*

phrases.he: כשעצמיות חפץ חסד שבה, שבהתכללות בבחינת היולי
phrases.en: like the inner *chesed* which is included as a *hiyuli*

phrases.he: כולל כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ ברצון של חסד פרטי כו'
phrases.en: which includes every particular *chesed* they're ever going to want to do

blocks.text: So now he explains it: the *ratzon kadum* is the source of every *ratzon l'ratzon*. It is understood by way of an example: **this is like the *yechida* of a person's soul**, the *yechida*, the *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul), with its *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness). It is **like the inner *chesed*** (kindness) **which is included as a *hiyuli***, and **which includes every particular *chesed* they're ever going to want to do**.

phrases.he: כאשר בא ונמשך בדרך פרט לדבר א'
phrases.en: when it now comes to a particular *ratzon*

phrases.he: ויוצא מבחינת העצמיות להיות לו רצון עצמי הנעלם שהוא בחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: so first it goes out of his *etzem* as this first *ratzon kadum*, that he has this inner urge to fulfill his desire for kindness, to express kindness

phrases.he: אבל עדיין בלתי מלובש באותו הדבר כלל,
phrases.en: It's not yet *meluvash* in it.

phrases.he: רק שהרצון הוא לעצמו עדיין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it's still for himself

blocks.text: **When it now comes to a particular *ratzon***: in the end his will for kindness comes to wanting to give a dollar to the poor person, or a coat to the freezing guy, or shoes, whatever it is. But **first it goes out of his *etzem*** (essence) **as this first *ratzon kadum***: he has an inner urge to fulfill his desire for kindness, to express kindness.

But it is not yet enclothed in anything. As soon as he opens the door and sees this guy freezing, like with the coat, right away his heart goes out to him and he wants to help. He wants this person to walk away happy. That is what he wants, but he is not yet thinking in terms of what he is looking for in the world.
blocks.title: The freezing man at the door

blocks.text: Like a guy who says he wants to get a present for somebody. "Well, what do you want?" He does not know yet what he wants; he does not know what he is looking for. It is an abstract thing: he wants the guy to be happy. Or as it describes the will for a house: he wants his friends to praise him. He does not know what kind of house will do that, but he will bring his friends over, show it off and feel good, and that feeling is what he is looking for. So too here: he is looking for the feeling of having done a nice thing, that this person should be helped.
blocks.title: A present for somebody, a house to show off

blocks.text: That is the point. **It's not yet *meluvash*** (enclothed) **in it**. It has not yet become a will for what will help this guy. He does not know yet what will help him; he does not know what the problem is. He just hears a guy crying, so his heart goes out to him, but he cannot yet know what he wants to do. He just wants the person to feel good. So **it's still for himself**: he wants the pain of hearing this person crying to go away, because he feels bad.

phrases.he: אך כאשר מלובש ופועל רצון לרצון בדבר הפרטי הזה,
phrases.en: but then, when it's *meluvash* in it, it effects a *ratzon l'ratzon* for this particular thing

phrases.he: כמו שמתלבש ופועל רצון לרצון בשכל ומחשבה בדבר פרט הזה,
phrases.en: that means that he now associates it in his *machshava*, in his *sechel*, he associates this inner desire with a particular thing, like to give him a coat

phrases.he: הרי התהוות זה הרצון שבשכל ומחשבה
לדבר זה הוא כמו התהוות בריאה חדשה ממקורו
phrases.en: this is like creating a new thing

phrases.he: והוא מפני שבחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל הוא המקור להתהוות הרצון לרצון הזה שבשכל כו',
phrases.en: This is the source for this associated *ratzon* in his *sechel*.

blocks.text: But then, **when it's *meluvash* in it, it effects a *ratzon l'ratzon* for this particular thing**. That means **that he now associates it in his *machshava*, in his *sechel***: he associates this inner desire with a particular thing, like giving him a coat. This is *davka* (specifically) in intellect and thought: he makes the association by evaluating the situation, he creates a certain picture of what will fulfill the will, and then it becomes a will for that.

Now his will is enclothed in that form, and **this is like creating a new thing**: he is now creating that this will should be for this form, for a coat. From the side of the light, the will for the coat was not there. But he has the ability to figure out what form would fit it, and that is also part of his essential *hiyuli*; from that side you could say the coat is actually there. And the *ratzon kadum* **is the source for this associated *ratzon* in his *sechel***.

sections.title: The will for a will is created: it comes and goes, it can be strong or weak, and a bribe can make it
sections.summary: Business and learning come and go because they are only a means to an end, so the connection between the essential will and the particular will is not essential: it is created, like a language, and has priorities. A bribe makes such a connection, and *Adam Kadmon* is the first and most general one, where the first mistake can be made.

phrases.he: ונקרא רצון לרצון זה בריאה
phrases.en: and this new associated *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the coat or whatever, is called like a created thing, something new

phrases.he: שהרי אנו רואים שלא בכל העתים יהיה לאדם רצון לרצון פרטי,
phrases.en: even if a person has the same essential *ratzon*, it's not always connected to the same *ratzon l'ratzon*

phrases.he: כמו הרצון במסחור או בלימוד
phrases.en: like the desire to do business or to learn

phrases.he: שבהכרח יש מקור המהווה לרצון זה הפרטי
ונקרא רצון לרצון זה,
phrases.en: and this inner *ratzon* is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon*, the inner desire that was powering and the source of this associated *ratzon*, this secondary *ratzon*

blocks.text: So **this new associated *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the coat or whatever, is called like a created thing, something new**. For we see that **even if a person has the same essential *ratzon*, it's not always connected to the same *ratzon l'ratzon***: **like the desire to do business or to learn**.

There must be a source that makes this particular will. A person does not always feel like working, and he does not always feel like learning and studying. Why? Because he is doing it only as a means to an end. A person does business only to make money. Once he has made money, he does not want to do business anymore. "Why? I thought you wanted to do this deal?" But if it is not going to accomplish his goal, he is not going to want to do it. The same with learning: if he wants to understand a certain thing, he will want to research and study. Once he has learned what he wanted to know, he does not just feel like learning anymore.
blocks.title: Business and learning are a means to an end

blocks.text: So the business and the learning are a secondary, associated will, **and this inner *ratzon* is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon***: the inner desire that was powering this associated will and is its source.

phrases.he: וממילא מובן מאחר שלא בכל העתים נמשך הרצון לרצון זה,
phrases.en: since the essential *ratzon* doesn't always come into this associated *ratzon*

phrases.he: וגם לפעמים יאיר אור רב ותקיף
phrases.en: and also sometimes it will shine very strongly, they'll want it very much

phrases.he: ולפעמים יאיר במיעוט וחלישות כו',
נמצא מוכרח שגם המקור העושה ומהוה לרצון זה, הנקרא רצון לרצון, הוא גם כן בא בבחינת התהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: even this association between the two things, which is the source, what connects the one *ratzon* to the other *ratzon*, that is also created

blocks.text: And so it is understood: **since the essential *ratzon* doesn't always come into this associated *ratzon***, **and also sometimes it will shine very strongly, they'll want it very much**, and sometimes weakly (sometimes he is really into doing the business, sometimes he just does it, whatever; the same with learning), it must be that the source that makes this will, called the *ratzon l'ratzon*, also comes as a creation, *yesh me'ayin*.

In other words, if the association between the one will and the other were essential, if the desire for kindness were essentially connected to the coat, it would always come out. The fact that sometimes it comes out and sometimes it does not, that the desire for money sometimes comes out as doing business and sometimes not, that the wish to know sometimes comes out as learning and sometimes not: why? Because they are not essentially connected. A person can have an inner will and not realize what it is for, or not know what will accomplish it; sometimes this accomplishes it, sometimes that. So **even this association between the two things, which is the source, what connects the one *ratzon* to the other *ratzon*, that is also created**. He has to create the association and decide that this should be connected to that.

It is like a person's *bittul* (self-nullification), his *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) to G-d, his *bittul* to the One whose will it is: it is connected to a particular thing only when He says that this is what He wants. If He says He wants something else, then it changes, and it will do that other thing.

So it can change, or it can be stronger, and you can also make a priority system: sometimes it is a stronger connection, sometimes a weaker one. If they were essentially connected, it would be all the same: this would equal that, and that is it. There would be no main thing and secondary thing, no higher and lower. But since this whole thing is created, it does not have to be this way; it could be another way. Therefore you can make this thing more connected and that thing less connected.

phrases.he: כמו השוחד,
phrases.en: and it's like a bribe

phrases.he: שיעשה רצון לרצון ושכל לזכות תמיד
phrases.en: that a bribe connects his *ratzon* for the money to the *ratzon* for this guy to be innocent

blocks.text: **And it's like a bribe**: **a bribe connects his *ratzon* for the money to the *ratzon* for this guy to be innocent**. It is not that his will for money is essentially connected to making this guy innocent. But the guy says, "I'll give you this money, but I'll make you a deal: I'll only give it to you if you do that." So now it becomes connected.

But there is no direct connection; it is just circumstantial, like when you make a language. That is the point: it is like making a language. Only this is creating a language within your will, as opposed to the actual creation of the details, which is when you make an actual language to speak to somebody, like English or Hebrew. This is how you speak to yourself, to communicate with yourself, to know what you want. But it is the same idea.

No, that is a will, as much as we use it; it is just not a *ratzon kadum*. The will for money is not an essential desire. *Ratzon kadum* means the essential psychological needs of all people, before anything that has to do with society or circumstance.
blocks.question: Is the desire for money a *ratzon kadum*?

blocks.text: There you are creating a *yosher*. *Yosher* means association; that is what *yosher* always means, when you associate things. It is creating a language: you take a bunch of *masachim* (screens), a bunch of things that are essential forms or whatever, you associate one to the other, and then you use them as a way to convey a light. That is the idea of a *yosher*. And by doing that you also create a hierarchy: this one is the main thing and that one is secondary, which is to think of higher and lower.

It is *mamash* (actually) like a language that you create. Take a word, let's say the word water. You take the thing, water, and you take that sound, and you connect the two. So there are three things here: there is water, there is the sound of the word water, and there is the ability to connect the two of them, to make a language, to associate them.
blocks.title: The word water

blocks.text: And this is the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*: it creates a *masach* (screen). A *masach* is like an interface, like a language, that lets you connect a light, to give it over to somebody else. That is the *bekia* (breaking through) of the *masach*: when you hear the words of the language, you are able to extract the intellect from them, and so the original intellect is able to shine through.

So a person's bank of knowledge of everything in the world around him, just the raw facts of his experience, are like the material for the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, and the way you make it into a structure is like a body. The *igulim* are like the soul, and this knowledge is like the body. And the way you see them connecting, the way you connect them, is the *ratzon l'ratzon*.

That connection means that when you want something inside your essence, which is like the *igulim*, a spiritual thing, it does not automatically connect to a certain thing in the world, the way your power of intellect gets connected to your brain (as we will talk about later with the lights and vessels of *Atzilus*). This is the same relationship in every world between the *igulim* and the *yosher*: like a soul to a body, or lights to vessels.

But the unique thing in *Adam Kadmon* is that this is the original and general association of all your wills with the general form. The later ones are the associations of how you are going to get it, or of different things according to circumstances, which are more detailed. That is why it is called the seventy years of a person's life: this is the most general form a person makes of who he is.

And this is the first opportunity a person has to make a mistake, because here he needs an interpretation. The facts, everybody knows: he knows what he wants, and he knows the outside world. But if there is a mistake in how the two fit together, that is where the source of a *shevira* (the breaking of the vessels) is.

There is a process of this when the soul is put into the body, and a person also does it himself: as soon as he is born he starts to create his self-image and his worldview. There is a deeper *hishtalshelus* within the soul itself, but within the soul as it is enclothed in the body there is also this whole *hishtalshelus*. That is the real *mashal*: what we really understand is the way the *hishtalshelus* works in the vital soul, the animal soul, once the soul goes into the body, and that is the *mashal* we always use for everything. When a person is a little kid, until about five, he creates this self-image and worldview, and based on that his personality is decided for the rest of his life, and it is very hard to change.

blocks.text: But the same thing really happens to the soul before it comes into the body, the G-dly soul: it is shown the sparks it is supposed to refine, and that gives it a certain form. The problem that happens there, the source of the *shevira*, is that each soul only sees its part of the plan, so there can come to be a separation. That is why you need an *eruv chatzeiros* (the joining of courtyards for Shabbos) to connect private domains ("how do you say it? I don't know how you say it in plural"). A private domain means that his four cubits are all for holiness: he is whole in his service of G-d and uses everything for Torah and mitzvos. But it is only his personal thing, his proper way, the way he should serve G-d, right for him; and he does not understand that somebody else has a different nature and a different service.

blocks.text: If he is not able to understand that and connect the two, there can still be a separation, as the Mitteler Rebbe talks about in *Derech Chaim*: a separation between great, holy, whole rabbis. Historically there were always fights between such people. The fight between the Chassidim and the Misnagdim really started in the time of the Rishonim, with disputes about practical Kabbala, and then it became a dispute about Kabbala in general. It came down through the time of the Yaavetz and the Ramchal and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz and the Baal Shem Tov, all these people, and then the Gra and the Alter Rebbe; it was a whole process. The point was that the Misnagdim were Torah souls and the Chassidim were more *tefilla* (prayer) souls. That is what the Alter Rebbe said when the government was interrogating him: their service is more in Torah, and ours is more in *tefilla*. But the Misnagdim thought that not putting the emphasis on Torah was like heresy.
blocks.title: Chassidim and Misnagdim: Torah souls and tefilla souls

In the dispute between the Chassidim and the Misnagdim, the point was that the Misnagdim were Torah souls and the Chassidim were more *tefilla* (prayer) souls. blocks.text: There were other things involved too, and it got ugly as people got personally involved, and it became a whole *kelipa* (what conceals G-dliness). But the source of it was a thing in holiness. That kind of separation is already the root: each person has his own path in the service of G-d and does not see how it all connects to the same intention, and that leads to complete separation, until it is *mamash* baseless hatred, people actually just killing each other and making accusations against each other. "That's what happened." When that kind of separation came down to people who were not as holy, that is what came out of it. And that is how, even from the side of the G-dly soul, the source of this separation starts already there, depending on which part of *Adam Kadmon* the soul comes from.

blocks.text: That is why you need *davka* a leader, to connect everybody together. The head of the Jewish people, a Rebbe, is a general soul: he sees the whole picture, sees that each person has his own service, and that they are all details of the general thing. So he can tell each person what he is supposed to do and how they are all supposed to work together, and help unite everybody, until the general soul that unites everybody throughout all the generations: *Moshiach* himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: From the side of the vital soul, the problem is that a person grows up in a *goyishe* world, so he can get wrong ideas very easily. Or even in holiness: if a person grows up in a Jewish world, but the people around him take what is the right service for them to be the only right way and do not see past it, he can think he has to be like that person, and that is not really best for his own service. Eventually he will be disillusioned: he will try, and it will not work. Then if he does not realize that there is something deeper, that it does not have to be in that form, and find the right role model for himself, the right service, the right self-image of who he is supposed to be and how he fits in, then big problems.

blocks.text: This is a problem both on the side of *kelipa* and on the side of holiness. It is a thing you see teenagers struggle with, when they start trying to implement, to be, the self-image they had. They say they are trying to find themselves: how they fit into the picture, how they can actually be that.

blocks.text: That is also why stories are so important. When you hear stories of *tzaddikim* and Chassidim, or in general of great people who exemplify the thing, that gives you the image of the real purpose, the real final goal of how to bring the Torah down into life. There are different types of stories and different types of people. Each person can learn something from every story, but there is a certain type of person who is the hero he associates with, and that is who he tries to be like. Each person has certain stories that really inspire him, and he kind of lives by that message.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: And the whole purpose of the *maamarim* (discourses) and the like is that you should understand what was going on in the story, and how you can actually be like that, so that it does not become an external thing, just copying the external symptoms. It is easy to dress the same way as somebody; everybody does it. They get dressed like their role models. The same with sports stars and movie stars: people just get the paraphernalia. And Chassidim also copy people. It is the same idea: they see that person as who they want to be and try to copy it, but if they do not catch what the real thing behind it is, it is not going to get them there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: But as far as what we are talking about here: the will for the *dira b'tachtonim* became a will for a certain form, and *Adam Kadmon* is the source of the Torah and mitzvos and all these things, and also of the form of the world we live in. That is the *chitzoniyus*: G-d made the world according to a form. Which world is going to be the dwelling? Which lower place are we going to have? And the Torah and mitzvos are the *pnimiyus*: the will for how to make that lower place a dwelling. That is the source of everything. The same with the souls of Israel, how the souls are going to be: the souls become like a created being, and that happens in *Adam Kadmon*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 64 opens by carrying on the end of class 63 (on Adam Kadmon, self-image and the source of the shevira) and reads line 16 again only at w1724; placed under line 16, the passage class 63 stopped on.

blocks.text: Until then the soul is a part of G-d; it is not something separate. What is created is *davka* the form the soul takes on; the essence of the soul is not created. So the fact that everybody gets his form, the root of his soul, his mission and everything: the root of all of it is *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Like the bribe: if a person is bribed, the money is connected to his essential will, to something he wants. The bribe makes him have a personal interest. His will for himself, which in this case is already connected to money because of earlier things, now makes him feel connected; his intellect is now connected, so it is not objective anymore. Originally, the reason he was sitting there as a judge was that his interest was justice. By giving him a bribe, now he wants something for himself, and that twists his will for justice to fit his will for money. So it will make him always have a will for merit.

phrases.he: מפני שהשוחד מגיע בעצמות נפשו,
phrases.en: because the *shochad* connects his *etzem* to it

phrases.he: שמחמתו יומשך תמיד התהוות רצון לרצון של חסד וזכות
phrases.en: This will always cause that he'll have a bias now for *chesed* and for merit.

phrases.he: ולהיפך לשונאו
phrases.en: for his enemy

phrases.he: יתהווה תמיד רצון לרצון של דין כו' וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.
phrases.en: And for somebody that he hates, since he has a personal interest against the person, he'll always look to find him guilty and look negatively on him.

blocks.text: **Because the *shochad* connects his *etzem* to it**: the *shochad* (a bribe) reaches the essence of his soul, and so it **will always cause that he'll have a bias now for *chesed* and for merit**. And the reverse, **for his enemy**: for somebody he hates, since he has a personal interest against the person, he will always look to find him guilty and look negatively on him.

sections.title: Ten wills for a will: Adam Kadmon as the hidden source of the wills of Atzilus
sections.summary: Every revealed will has ten, so a person makes ten associations, a whole self-image; a Jew's real self-image is to do whatever is needed. So too the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are only *ratzon l'ratzon*, the hidden source of the revealed *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: G-d decided to reveal Himself as wise and as a creator.

phrases.he: וידוע דכל רצון גלוי כלול מי'.
phrases.en: every revealed *ratzon* has ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: אם כן גם הרצון לרצון זה כלול מי'
phrases.en: it must also have ten

phrases.he: ויש י' כחות, ממילא יש י' מיני רצון לרצון,
phrases.en: There's ten, you have to make ten associations

phrases.he: שמתהווים כולם בבחינת יש מאין כו'
phrases.en: it creates each of these *ratzonos* in a way of *yesh me'ayin*, that it creates from the abstract *ratzon* the concrete thing

blocks.text: It is known that **every revealed *ratzon* has ten *sefiros***, so the will for a will **must also have ten**. In other words: how do you know how to make the intellect and the emotions and everything go? For each of them you have to create an image that connects your essential will, which we said has ten in a hidden way, to it. A kid's will for a home is a certain feeling, and that feeling is going to have a say in every single aspect of the house: how he wants the kitchen, the dining room, the living room, everything.

And there are ten powers. **There's ten, you have to make ten associations**: every person has to figure out how he sees his intellect, his *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding), his *chesed*, everything. He has to create a whole self-image: how he sees himself in the classroom, how he sees himself on the sports field, what he wants for each of those things, and how it all fits together. So different people can make different wills.

Some people make a self-image like the saying of the Rebbe Rashab: a *maskil* is a guy who learns all day, and an *oved* is a guy who *davens* all day. Who is an *oved* and a *maskil*? The one who peels potatoes for the *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering). Why? A person whose self-image is totally in one thing gets rid of everything else. If he wants to be a *maskil*, he only wants to learn; he does not have time to *daven*. If a guy wants to be an *oved* and just *daven*, he does not have time to learn. But if a guy's will is to do whatever G-d wants, then whatever needs to be done right now, he does: if it is time to learn he learns, if it is time to *daven* he *davens*, and if he needs to peel potatoes for the *farbrengen*, he does that too.
blocks.title: Who is a maskil and an oved? The one who peels potatoes

blocks.text: So that is what a Jew is. A Jew's real inner will, the real self-image of a Jew, is someone who is able to do anything, who is flexible: *davka* whatever needs to be done, he will do.

And the *goyim* (the nations) are all set in a certain order: they have a will to be like this and like that, and that is their thing. That is why they have a *mazal* (a ruling star), the *mazal* for each one.

sensitivity.reason: Speaks of "the goyim" as all set in their ways ("that's their thing"), against the Jew's flexibility; the teaching behind it is the mazal of each nation.
sensitivity.publishable: The nations, by contrast, are each set in a certain order: each has a will to be like this or like that. That is the idea of the *mazal* (a ruling star) for each one.

blocks.text: And the will for a will **creates each of these *ratzonos* in a way of *yesh me'ayin***: it **creates from the abstract *ratzon* the concrete thing**. The something comes out from the nothing; in other words, it associates them.

phrases.he: וכל זה דוגמא להבין בבחינת עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, שכללותם ענין רצון לרצון לבד
phrases.en: The whole *inyan* of *Adam Kadmon* is the association of a *ratzon* to another *ratzon*.

phrases.he: שהרי הן בחינת ההעלם דעשר ספירות דאצילות שבגלוי כידוע
phrases.en: the *Adam Kadmon* is the *helem* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

blocks.text: And all this is an example to understand the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*. **The whole *inyan* of *Adam Kadmon* is the association of a *ratzon* to another *ratzon***: that is the whole *inyan* (matter) of it. And **the *Adam Kadmon* is the *helem* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus***, the *helem* (concealment) of what is revealed there. The revealed wills in *Atzilus* come as a desire to fulfill the general form that was created in *Adam Kadmon*, which is from the hidden will before it, the *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.he: וכמו כתר דחכמה דאצילות
phrases.en: the *ratzon* for *chachma* of *Atzilus*, which is like the *ratzon* for the *chachma* of the Torah

phrases.he: שהוא הרצון שבשכל כו'
phrases.en: that *Hashem* has a *ratzon* to make the Torah be the most amazing book ever

phrases.he: שרשו בכתר שבחכמה דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: the source of that is in the *Keser sheb'chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שנקרא רצון לרצון זה
phrases.en: which is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon*

phrases.he: וכן כתר שבחסד דאצילות
phrases.en: the *ratzon* for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, which is the *ratzon* to create this world

phrases.he: מכתר שבחסד דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: Which is like the *Keser* *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Like **the *ratzon* for *chachma* of *Atzilus*, which is like the *ratzon* for the *chachma* of the Torah**: **that *Hashem* has a *ratzon* to make the Torah be the most amazing book ever**, and to see the wisdom in creation too. That will to create intellect in the Torah and in the world comes from *Adam Kadmon*, because *Adam Kadmon* is the way G-d wants to reveal Himself.

He decided to reveal Himself as wise. If this is the real *nimshal*, really from G-d's side, then G-d decided to associate Himself with a certain form, the form of *Adam Kadmon*: "the G-d form", the highest form we have. Since He decided to reveal Himself as the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*, as the G-d of intellect, that makes a will to reveal it by revealing wisdom in the world. And **the source of that is in the *Keser sheb'chachma* of *Adam Kadmon***, the *Keser* within *chachma*, **which is called the *ratzon* for this *ratzon***.

And so too **the *ratzon* for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, which is the *ratzon* to create this world**, to actually create a particular thing: the will to create a particular thing comes from the will to reveal Himself as a creator, which is like **the *Keser* *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon***. In other words, *Adam Kadmon* is the essential association of His essential will, which is the real *ratzon kadum*, with how to reveal Himself. First He creates this picture of what He is going to reveal of Himself, and based on that He knows how He is going to reveal Himself in the world.

sections.title: From the Kav: only one of the ways the primordial will could come out, and all of it hidden
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from the *Kav*, the essential will, which chose this form as a vessel and makes a will for every detail, from *Keser* to *Malchus*. But *Adam Kadmon* is only the outer side of the *ratzon kadum*, one way out of many, and it is all hidden: a subconscious association, like a language learned before one speaks.

phrases.he: ואמנם התהוות עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון עצמו,
phrases.en: but where did these *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from?

phrases.he: הכל נמשך מבחינת הקו שנקרא מקור התהוות כל הרצונות לרצונות כו'
phrases.en: These are all from the *Kav*

phrases.he: להיותו עצם הרצון הפשוט שקדם בעצמו שיהיה כך כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: they all come from the *ratzon kadum*, which is the *etzem ratzon*

blocks.text: But **where did these *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from?** **These are all from the *Kav***. G-d picks this form, the way a teacher makes a plan of how the intellect is going to come out, with a hierarchy: what is the beginning, what is the next level. So too G-d chose this form, and so this is also a revelation of His essence, because He chose this form to be the vessel for the light.

The *Kav* is called the source of the coming into being of all the wills, and **they all come from the *ratzon kadum*, which is the *etzem ratzon***, the essential will. These are all just a vessel to serve it.

phrases.he: על כן הוא פועל ועושה רצון לרצון בדרך פרט
phrases.en: Therefore, since this *etzem ratzon* also comes in to create a *ratzon* for every *prat*

phrases.he: והוא מבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון עד בחינת מלכות שבו,
phrases.en: the whole *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* from *Keser* to *Malchus*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת רצון לרצון דמלוכה כו'
phrases.en: which *Malchus* is the *ratzon l'ratzon* for *melucha*

blocks.text: So it makes a will for a will in a particular way. **Therefore, since this *etzem ratzon* also comes in to create a *ratzon* for every *prat***, every *prat* (detail), as we said about the house, it becomes enclothed in each detail, for how that detail will fit into the essential will.

These particular wills are **the whole *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* from *Keser* to *Malchus***. And *Malchus* **is the *ratzon l'ratzon* for *melucha*** (kingship): G-d wants to reveal Himself as king, and that creates the will to have separate beings who feel that they can do what they want, and who listen to G-d only because they have to, because He is the king.

phrases.he: ואמנם רק מבחינת אחרונה שברצון הקדום ההיולי הנזכר לעיל נעשה בחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: but *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum*

blocks.text: But the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is **only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum***. In other words, this is only one way that it could be expressed. It is not really essential; that is the point. *Adam Kadmon* does not really grasp the full *ratzon kadum*, because the *ratzon kadum* could come out another way.

Take a guy who wants to be the rich guy with the big house. In America, the will is for a nice brick mansion with a nice lawn and a Cadillac or whatever. In another society, let's say in Africa, it is for a hut, or two huts and a couple of cows. The will for a house also depends on where you are. In Israel they make houses out of stone so they will be cool, because they do not have so much wood there and it is very hot; they make them specially to fit where they are. In America they make them with insulation to keep out the cold. It is a different type of thing. So the picture of *Adam Kadmon* is just one little way the essential will could come out; it could come out many ways.
blocks.title: A mansion, two huts, a stone house

sensitivity.reason: Uses a stock picture of Africa (a hut, two huts and a couple of cows) as the contrast to an American mansion.

phrases.he: שהוא רצון לרצון הנעלם שלמעלה מחכמה שברצון לרצון הנעלם כו'
phrases.en: the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is the *ratzon* to create this form, the associations, which is higher than the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה כל עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, הכל בבחינת ההעלם
phrases.en: It's all *b'helem*, meaning that it's all like a subconscious thing

phrases.he: ורצון לרצון לכל עשר ספירות דאצילות שבא בבחינת גלוי,
כמו שיתבאר ודי למבין:
phrases.en: we'll explain the next *perek* how the *ratzonos* of *Atzilus* come out from *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: Only from the *chitzoniyus* of the *ratzon kadum* does it become the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, which is the hidden will for a will. So **the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* is the *ratzon* to create this form, the associations, which is higher than the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon***.

And so all ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*: **it's all *b'helem*** (hidden), **meaning that it's all like a subconscious thing**. *Adam Kadmon* is not yet an actual will. It is like when you learn a language. When you learn a language you are not actually saying anything yet; you just know that when you want to talk about this, this is the word you would use. In the same way, *Adam Kadmon* is just creating the association: when you want a house, this is the house you want.

You create that when you are a little kid, really. But you do not want the house until you are, let's say, twenty-five or something. The will for the will was already set up; it was just a hidden will. It is like a subconscious association.

Or like with commercials: they try to set it up so that you associate your essential will, for being thirsty, say, with Coca-Cola. Then, when you actually come to a situation where you are thirsty, you will buy their thing. But the inner connection between the two is a subconscious thing, and that is why it is called a hidden will.
blocks.title: Thirsty, so Coca-Cola

blocks.text: As for the will for a will of all the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, which comes as revelation: **we'll explain the next *perek*** (chapter) **how the *ratzonos* of *Atzilus* come out from *Adam Kadmon***.

sections.title: Why Adam Kadmon is called Beriya and thought, and the Kav that is above it
sections.summary: *Adam Kadmon* is the man of *Beriya* because the will for a will is created according to circumstances, and it starts in thought: the will associated with a picture. Its *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* make the associations in a hidden thought. The *Kav* is higher: an essential will that knows everything by knowing itself, as the Rambam says.

phrases.he: וזהו שבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו',
phrases.en: this is why *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, the creation

phrases.he: כמו בחינת התהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: it's creating something from nothing

phrases.he: כנראה בחוש שהתהוות הרצון לרצון לעתים מיוחדים הוא בא, כשאר התהוות איזה מציאות כו'
phrases.en: that the *ratzon haratzon* is created according to the circumstances, like any other *metzius* that's not an essential thing

blocks.text: And **this is why *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, the creation**: **it's creating something from nothing**. The will for a will **is created according to the circumstances, like any other *metzius* that's not an essential thing**.

phrases.he: והוא כמו התהוות המחשבה,
phrases.en: It's like creation of a *machshava*

phrases.he: שהיא התהוות יש מאין לגבי עצמיות הרצון שבנפשו
phrases.en: like when you make a language, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain thought

phrases.he: כנראה בחוש שהרצון לרצון הבא בבחינת התהוות כנזכר לעיל,
תחלת התהוותו במחשבה דוקא
phrases.en: and this is first done in *machshava*, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain form, a certain picture

phrases.he: כי המחשבה בחינת כלי לרצון,
phrases.en: the *machshava* is a *kli* for the *ratzon*

phrases.he: שהרצון מתלבש במחשבה,
phrases.en: that your *ratzon* becomes associated with a certain picture, a certain thought

phrases.he: כמו וחשב לעשות כו'
phrases.en: like it says, he thought to do

phrases.he: וכן תחלת התהוות רצון לרצון במחשבה,
phrases.en: and so too the beginning of the *ratzon haratzon* also is in *machshava*

phrases.he: הוא שנקרא רצון שבמחשבה כו'
phrases.en: this is called the *ratzon* within the *machshava*

blocks.text: **It's like creation of a *machshava***, a thought: it is **like when you make a language, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain thought**. So when you want something, you will think, oh, and you will picture a certain thing. We see it works like a language: the will for a will also comes into being, **and this is first done in *machshava*, that you associate your *etzem haratzon* with a certain form, a certain picture**.

For **the *machshava* is a *kli* for the *ratzon***: the thought is a *kli* (vessel) for the will. The will is enclothed in thought, meaning **that your *ratzon* becomes associated with a certain picture, a certain thought**, **like it says, he thought to do**. And **so too the beginning of the *ratzon haratzon* also is in *machshava***. That is why it is called thought: dealing with *Adam Kadmon*, it is in a thought. And **this is called the *ratzon* within the *machshava***: when your will becomes associated with a certain thought.

phrases.he: וזהו כללות ענין כח''ב דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: the *inyan* of the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת התהוות פעולת אור רצון לרצון דרך פרט
phrases.en: the *KaChaB* of *Adam Kadmon* is what creates the association

phrases.he: שבא במחשבה סתימאה כו'
phrases.en: which come out from the *machshava stima'a*

blocks.text: And this is **the *inyan* of the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Adam Kadmon***: **the *KaChaB* of *Adam Kadmon* is what creates the association**. That is where you make the associations, and the *middos* (emotional attributes) of *Adam Kadmon* are the effect: once you make these associations, that means I will want this and I will not want that, and everything like that. They **come out from the *machshava stima'a***, the hidden thought. It means that it is a subconscious association; that is why it is called *stima'a*, hidden.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בבחינת הקו עצמו שלמעלה מבחינת פעולת התהוות רצון לרצון לדבר פרט במחשבה סתימאה גם כן כו'
phrases.en: but the *Kav* was higher than being associated even in *machshava stima'a* with any sort of a *ratzon*

phrases.he: רק לעצמו עדיין
phrases.en: It's just an essential desire for you to feel a certain way, not connected to any picture or something outside.

phrases.he: חושב כל מה שיהיה כו'
phrases.en: you just think of everything that will be, in an abstract, in an essential way

phrases.he: שכולל במחשבת עצמו עדיין
phrases.en: and it's so included in his own *machshava*

phrases.he: ולא בהתהוות רצון במחשבה שחוץ ממנו כלל ודי למבין
phrases.en: and not in a creation or association of something outside of him at all

phrases.he: (ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו בידיעת עצמו ולא בידיעה שחוץ ממנו וכו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר):

blocks.text: But **the *Kav* was higher than being associated even in *machshava stima'a* with any sort of a *ratzon***. **It's just an essential desire for you to feel a certain way, not connected to any picture or something outside**: **you just think of everything that will be, in an abstract, in an essential way**.

It is **so included in his own *machshava***, **and not in a creation or association of something outside of him at all**. In the Rambam's words: by knowing Himself, and not by a knowledge outside of Him. That is *yedias atzmo* (self-knowledge): since you know yourself, you automatically know what you want. That is the idea of the *ratzon kadum*. And *Adam Kadmon* is already a knowledge outside of Him.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* called a creation *yesh me'ayin*, and what is the true *ayin* it comes from?
In the example of the man at the door, what is still *ratzon kadum* and what has become a *ratzon l'ratzon*?
How does the fact that a person does not always want to do business or to learn show that the *ratzon l'ratzon* is created?
What does a bribe do to a judge, and why does it make him look for merit, or for guilt in his enemy?
Why is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* only from the outer side of the *ratzon kadum*, and what do the houses in different countries show?
How is the *Kav* different from the *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*, and what do the Rambam's words about knowing Himself add?

notes.text: The machine hears ratzon l'ratzon as "ratzon v'ratzon" in classes 62 and 63 and as "ratzon sheb'ratzon" or "ratzon haratzon" in class 65. The prose writes *ratzon l'ratzon* throughout; the phrase of line 7 (62 w757-762, heard "ratzon v'ratzon") is written *ratzon l'ratzon*, and the phrases of lines 35, 39 keep *ratzon haratzon* as heard.

63 w1654-1707 ("No, that's a ratzon... not actually a ratzon kadum") answers a question that is not on the tape. Written as a question block with askedBy student and the question inferred from the answer ("Is the desire for money a ratzon kadum?"). A reviewer should listen.

Class 64 opens (w0-1723) carrying on the end of class 63 about Adam Kadmon, the self-image and the source of the shevira (the soul's descent, Chassidim and Misnagdim, the leader, role models, stories), before rereading line 16. All of it is placed under line 16 with outOfPlace.

The history of the Chassidim and Misnagdim (64 w366-606) is as he gives it: that it began in the time of the Rishonim over practical Kabbala, then through the Yaavetz, the Ramchal, Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz, the Baal Shem Tov, the Gra and the Alter Rebbe; and the Alter Rebbe's answer under interrogation. *Derech Chaim* is cited as he cites it. A reviewer may want to check the history. He joins into one process controversies usually told apart (the Yaavetz and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz disputed over amulets, before the Chassidim and Misnagdim), and the killing at 64 w725 is his word; both are left as he says them, and the public version leaves out the history, the heresy remark and the killing.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the start and end of line 1, the middle of line 11 ("harei hishavus zeh haratzon sheb'sechel u'machshava"), the first half of line 14, the weak half of line 15 (his gloss there is about business, not a rendering), the first half of line 33, the first half of line 37, and line 44 (at 65 w2352-2371 he explains it rather than translating it). The English of line 27 (65 w1123-1137) and of line 28 (w1163-1181) is his explanation right after he reads them.
The line 3 mark (62 w204) falls mid-sentence on the line 2 explanation; he reads line 3 at w246. The first phrase of line 3 cites w237-245, said just before the reading.
"It says" that Adam Kadmon is like the seventy years of a person's life, and that Adam Kadmon is Moshiach (62 w1540-1682, 63 w2260-2291): he gives no source; kept as he says it.

Sensitivity, since Rabbi Walters has allowed a public edition: the flags on 64 w366-606, w607-791, w896-1091 and 65 w480-518, w1361-1545 replace only the history and the heresy remark, the killing, the word goyishe, the goyim remark (kept as the mazal of each nation, an ordinary Torah position) and Africa. Left unflagged as Torah positions: the Alter Rebbe as a Moshiach soul higher than Adam HaRishon, a Rebbe as a general soul, Chassidim copying people's dress.
